capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 of the last 3 under every candidate tag the engine reads, because AMH (a single-family rental REIT) reports its recurring real-estate capex on the cash-flow line 'Payments for capital improvements', tagged us-gaap PaymentsForCapitalImprovements, which is not in the engine's candidate tag list. Filed values in the FY2025 10-K: $40,137,000 (FY2023), $34,052,000 (FY2024), $40,645,000 (FY2025). The engine applies this single value to every missing period; the value used is the median of the three filed years. Against the true per-year figures it overstates FY2024 capex by $6,085,000 (conservative direction, lowers that year's OE) and understates FY2025 capex by $508,000 (negligible). Excluded, deliberately: acquisition and development spend on rental homes is growth investment presented separately by the filer, not the recurring capital-improvements line; charging it as capex would double-count growth.
capex_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-20, accession 0001562401-26-000010), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Payments for capital improvements' (us-gaap PaymentsForCapitalImprovements): $40,645,000 FY2025, $34,052,000 FY2024, $40,137,000 FY2023

moat_against: No network effects or tenant switching costs — leases are typically 12 months, rent is set by the local market, and a tenant can move to a competing home or apartment at renewal

Single-family rental supply is overwhelmingly fragmented mom-and-pop stock; AMH's scale is operating efficiency, not a barrier — Invitation Homes and other institutional landlords replicate the model with capital
Returns are capped by replacement cost and cap-rate arbitrage — new build-for-rent supply is the permanent competitor, including AMH's own development channel

Filed returns are thin: ROE ran 3.5% in 2021 to 7.3% in 2025 (fundamentals.json) and roic_proxy / gross margin are not computable from the filed presentation — no evidence of sustained returns well above the cost of capital
Political and regulatory scrutiny of institutional single-family landlords is a live, recurring risk (partly eased by the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, per Q2 2026 coverage)
moat_for: Scale and local density as an integrated owner-operator: professionally managed SFR platform with in-house leasing, renovation and property management lowering per-home turn and maintenance costs vs fragmented landlords

AMH Development Program — a genuine differentiator vs peers who must buy existing homes: more than 15,000 homes delivered since inception, 651 delivered in Q2 2026 (542 to the wholly owned portfolio), at initial yields management and outside coverage put above acquisition cap rates
Structural demand tailwind: high cost of homeownership keeps rent-vs-own economics favorable — Same-Home occupancy 96.0% in Q2 2026 with blended lease spreads +2.7% (renewals +3.2%, new leases +1.4%)

Expense discipline and balance-sheet access: controllable expense growth held below 1% YTD through Q2 2026, net debt/Adjusted EBITDA ~5.2x including preferreds, and buyback capacity used in Q2 2026 (4.1M shares repurchased at $29.88 average)
moat_justification: Scale, local density and the in-house development program are real but modest advantages in a commodity business: rent is a market price, leases are annual with no lock-in, fragmented mom-and-pop supply dominates, and new build-for-rent supply caps returns at replacement cost. Filed returns confirm it — ROE only 3.5% (2021) to 7.3% (2025) in fundamentals.json, with roic_proxy and gross margin not computable from the filed presentation — not the sustained well-above-cost-of-capital record a 7+ moat requires. Moat 4/10 (weak), the same score as direct peer Invitation Homes.
name: American Homes 4 Rent
one_liner: Quality single-family rental REIT, moat 4/10 — scale, local density and the in-house AMH Development Program are real but rent is a market price on 12-month leases and filed ROE is only 7.3%; on a TTM owner's-earnings base of $2.20/share after charging filed capital-improvements capex, weighted IRR is 10.4% (IV@15% $19.52) at $31.28, so it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$19.52 — the REIT lens (FY2026 Core FFO guided at $1.95/share, DPS TTM $1.26) is kinder than the OE lens, but neither supports 15% at this price.
